title: Northloop Payments Payout Rules: Account State, Payable Amount and Bank Change Hold
content:
This is the Northloop Payments rule on when a payout may leave a payments account and what may be paid.

## Clauses

1. Payouts may be sent only while the account is active or closing.
2. The payable amount is the balance less the reserved balance. The balance is the total seller balance on the payments account, reserved funds included, and it may go negative; the reserved balance is the part of the balance held back and not yet payable.
3. ~~A payout is sent on each scheduled payout day when the payable amount is at least the plan's minimum payout, for no more than the plan's maximum per payout.~~ **This clause is no longer in force**; the scheduled payout is governed by the current scheduled payout basis of Northloop Payments.
4. No payout is sent during the bank change payout hold counted in calendar days from the bank change date.
5. ~~On a plan that allows on-demand payouts the seller may request one standard payout of the payable amount when at least the on-demand interval has passed since the last on-demand payout.~~ **This clause is no longer in force**; on-demand payouts are governed by the current on-demand payout basis of Northloop Payments.
6. A closing account sends one final payout of the entire balance once its final hold has ended.
7. A balance of zero or below is never paid out.

## Account state (clause 1)

The state is read from the payments account record of the account the payout is sent from, not from what the seller says about it.

| Account state | Payout may be sent |
|---|---|
| active | yes |
| closing | yes |
| pending verification | no |
| on hold | no |
| closed | no |

## Bank change payout hold (clause 4)

- **Clock start:** the bank change date on the payments account record, that is the date the new bank account was verified.
- **Length:** the plan's bank change payout hold days, counted in calendar days.
- **Comparison:** a payout may be sent on a date not earlier than the bank change date plus the hold days; the day on which that sum falls is itself outside the hold, so equality satisfies the rule. Every earlier day is inside the hold and no payout is sent.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, plan with a 3-day hold, bank change date D):*

| Payout date | Inside the hold? |
|---|---|
| D plus 2 calendar days | yes, no payout is sent |
| D plus 3 calendar days | no, a payout may be sent |

On Payments Starter, whose hold is 7 days, the same reading gives D plus 6 inside the hold and D plus 7 outside it.

## Hypothetical payable amount

A balance of 1250.00 USD with 400.00 USD reserved gives a payable amount of 850.00 USD. A balance of minus 30.00 USD is below zero and is never paid out.

superseded_clauses: a payout is sent on each scheduled payout day when the payable amount is at least the plan's minimum payout, for no more than the plan's maximum per payout.
On a plan that allows on-demand payouts the seller may request one standard payout of the payable amount when at least the on-demand interval has passed since the last on-demand payout.
